commits.subject: State OS/2 version 1, as the release has
commits.body: All four released styles have an OS/2 version 1 table without USE_TYPO_METRICS (FontForge 2008-08-08 export); these files say OS2Version 0, which a converter reads as 'latest' and sets fsSelection bit 7. The obliques are generated from these files below and inherit it.

commits.subject: Drop the empty uni00A0 the 2010 re-save added
commits.body: None of the released styles maps U+00A0 or has a glyph for it. This .sfd ends with an empty uni00A0 (advance 637 in the regular, the last glyph id), which the 2010 re-save added after the 0.02 release; built, it would map U+00A0. The obliques are generated from these files below and inherit the drop.

commits.subject: Start src/Thabit-Oblique.sfd as a copy of src/Thabit.sfd
commits.body:
google/fonts ships Thabit as Arabeyes' Thabit 0.02 release (2008-08-09), whose fonts were made by src/build.py (helper.py in the 0.02 ChangeLog): it merges Thabit.fea and IBM Courier into the .sfd and, for the obliques, skews a copy of it. The source state those fonts were exported from is not archived; this .sfd is a 2010 re-save with the same drawing. Each step of the script is written into the .sfd as its own commit, so that the converted source builds what ships.

build.py's obliqize() opens src/Thabit.sfd and saves the skewed font as a temporary file, which generate() then exports. That intermediate is committed here as a source of its own, starting as an exact copy; the next commits make the script's changes.

commits.subject: Name src/Thabit-Oblique.sfd as build.py's obliqize() does
commits.body: obliqize() sets fontname to the upright's plus '-Oblique', fullname plus ' Oblique', familyname to 'Oblique' and appends the Arabic (Egypt) subfamily name 'maa'il' (here in UTF-7, as FontForge stores it). The release's PostScript name is Thabit-Oblique.

commits.subject: Start src/Thabit-BoldOblique.sfd as a copy of src/Thabit-Bold.sfd

The source state those fonts were exported from is not archived; this .sfd is a 2010 re-save with the same drawing. Each step of the script is written into the .sfd as its own commit, so that the converted source builds what ships.

build.py's obliqize() opens src/Thabit-Bold.sfd and saves the skewed font as a temporary file, which generate() then exports. That intermediate is committed here as a source of its own, starting as an exact copy; the next commits make the script's changes.

commits.subject: Name src/Thabit-BoldOblique.sfd as build.py's obliqize() does
commits.body: obliqize() sets fontname to the upright's plus '-Oblique', fullname plus ' Oblique', familyname to 'Bold Oblique' and appends the Arabic (Egypt) subfamily name 'areed maa'il' (here in UTF-7, as FontForge stores it). The release's PostScript name is Thabit-Bold-Oblique.

commits.subject: Skew the obliques as build.py's obliqize() does
commits.body: obliqize() selects every glyph worth outputting except afii61664..afii61575 (U+200C..U+202E, the joiners and bidi controls), unlinks references and transforms by psMat.skew(-16). psMat.skew takes RADIANS, so x' = x + tan(-16) y = x - 0.30063 y; the release measures -0.3007. Points are rounded to 1/1024 as FontForge 2008's TransformPoint() does, in single precision; anchors move with the outline. Done to the text by tools/ff_build_ops.py.

ops: cour/cour.pfa parenleft parenright exclam bracketleft bracketright braceleft braceright
commits.subject: Paste upright Courier brackets and exclam, as build.py's deobliqize() does
commits.body: deobliqize() copies ( ) [ ] { } and ! from the upright src/cour/cour.pfa over the skewed font, so the release draws them unskewed with the upright advance and side bearing. The glyphs are new here (the source has no Latin yet), encoded at their Unicode slots.

ops: cour/courb.pfa parenleft parenright exclam bracketleft bracketright braceleft braceright
commits.subject: Paste upright Courier brackets and exclam, as build.py's deobliqize() does
commits.body: deobliqize() copies ( ) [ ] { } and ! from the upright src/cour/courb.pfa over the skewed font, so the release draws them unskewed with the upright advance and side bearing. The glyphs are new here (the source has no Latin yet), encoded at their Unicode slots.

commits.subject: Merge Thabit.fea, as build.py does
commits.body: generate() runs font.mergeFeature('Thabit.fea'), which adds the whole GSUB: rligTashkilLigatures, InitialForms, MedialForms, FinalForms and ligaLamAlef, each with one subtable named as FontForge names it; the release's PfEd table names the same lookups and subtables. The .sfd itself has no GSUB.

commits.subject: Merge IBM Courier from src/cour/cour.pfa, as build.py does
commits.body:
generate() runs font.mergeFonts('cour/cour.pfa'): every Courier glyph that draws something and that the font lacks is copied in, unscaled (A keeps its 600-unit advance in the 1024-unit em), with seac accents as two references, named and encoded by FontForge 2008's UniFromName (SM680000 -> U+2310, ohm -> U+2126, micro -> U+00B5, ...). This is where the release's 458 Latin, Greek and box-drawing codepoints come from; the .sfd says 'Removed non-arabic glyphs' (ChangeLog 2008-08-09).

FontForge converted each copied cubic outline to quadratics with SplineSetsTTFApprox (splineorder2.c), which is not ported; tools/ff_build_ops.py uses fontTools' cu2qu with a maximum error of 1 unit instead, so the Latin points differ from the release's within about a unit.

ops: "Courier-'liga' Standard Ligatures in Latin lookup 0" ff=f+f fi=f+i fl=f+l ffi=ff+i ffl=ff+l
commits.subject: Add the f-ligature lookup FontForge read from IBM's cour.afm
commits.body: FontForge reads the .afm beside a Type 1 font it opens and turns its ligature lines into a 'liga' lookup for script latn (splinesaveafm.c LoadKerningDataFromAfm); the release has that lookup, named in its PfEd table "Courier-'liga' Standard Ligatures in Latin lookup 0". The AFMs are not in this tree. Their ligatures are stated here from X.Org font-ibm-type1 88a51daabc8a cour.afm, whose .pfa files are byte-identical to src/cour/: 'N f ; L f ff ; L i fi ; L l fl' and 'N ff ; L i ffi ; L l ffl'.

commits.subject: Restore the family name Thabit
commits.body: Every released style has typographic family 'Thabit' (name ID 16), and google/fonts METADATA names the family Thabit. The 2010 re-save of the uprights says FamilyName 'Regular' and 'Bold', and build.py's obliqize() sets 'Oblique' and 'Bold Oblique'.

commits.subject: State the release's English names
commits.body: The release names this style 'Thabit-Bold' (name ID 1), 'Thabit-Bold Bold' (ID 4) and 'Thabit' (ID 16, typographic family). ID 1 is what FontForge 2008 exported from the lost 0.02 source state (the Arabeyes 0.02 tarball has it too); ID 4 was rewritten in the binary by Raph Levien's FixName (googlefontdirectory-hg 465c5490a and 49339cae0, 2011-12-15), the only change google/fonts made to these fonts. Stated as LangName 1033 strings, which FontForge exports in preference to the derived names.

commits.subject: State the Arabic family name the release has
commits.body: Every Thabit release states name ID 1 (3,1,0x0C01) as U+062B U+0627 U+0628 U+062A, the Arabic full name this file already gives as ID 4; this file's Arabic record leaves ID 1 empty. Written in UTF-7 (+BisGJwYoBioA), as FontForge stores it. Value copied from google/fonts 538fa260b ofl/thabit/*.ttf.

commits.subject: Take Phi's quadratic outline from the release
commits.body: FontForge converted the merged IBM Courier glyphs to quadratic curves with its own approximation; the mergepsfont edit uses cu2qu, which reproduces every Latin glyph within rounding except Phi (5 px at 128 ppem). Points copied from google/fonts 90abd17b4 ofl/thabit/Thabit-Oblique.ttf.

disclose: The release's head.fontDirectionHint is 0 (FontForge writes 0 for a font with both left-to-right and right-to-left glyphs); fontc always writes 2, the value the OpenType specification now requires for this deprecated field. No renderer reads it. Decided 2026-10-02: disclose.
The release carries FontForge's private PfEd table (lookup, subtable and anchor-class names only). No shaper or rasterizer reads it and fontc does not write it. Decided 2026-10-02: disclose.

Thabit-Oblique and Thabit-BoldOblique are not flagged italic (and BoldOblique not bold) in OS/2 fsSelection and head.macStyle, while the releases are: FontForge took those bits from the style part of the font name; fontc takes them only from the italic angle or a master named Italic/Bold/Bold Italic, and a .glyphs source cannot state them otherwise. Needs a fontc change; planned as later work. Decided 2026-10-02: disclose.
